tagline: Up the middle of the peninsula, water on both sides.
intro: Out of Traverse City, M-37 takes Center Road up the spine of the Old Mission Peninsula, which splits Grand Traverse Bay into its East and West arms and is only about three and a quarter miles across at its widest. The road keeps to the ridge, through orchards, vineyards and farms, with a view of each arm of the bay, and ends at a cul-de-sac in front of a lighthouse.

Before the state built Center Road in the early 1940s, the way up was by narrow shoreline roads. The county's first public road ran from Traverse City to Old Mission in 1853, and in 1935 it was named Queen's Highway, for the cherry blossom queen.

moments.title: Old Mission
moments.text: The Presbyterian missionary Peter Dougherty founded a mission on this small harbor in 1839, moved it across the bay in 1852, and left the old place its name.

moments.title: Mission Point Light
moments.text: Built in 1870 as an exact copy of a Detroit River light since destroyed, it stands a few hundred yards short of the 45th parallel, halfway to the North Pole.

sources.label: MDOT, Pure Michigan Byways Driving Guide (Wayback Machine snapshot, December 2025)
